seeded-streaming-conversation.description: the 'Streaming' conversation seeded by holo seed:e2e --reset, with a durable message thread ready for streaming replies
records: 1 'Streaming' conversation exists in Postgres with >=1 prior message
the conversation has a non-empty conversation_id
Zero query chatMessagesByConversation returns >=1 message for this conversation

would_fail_if: stub — tokens from a hardcoded array, no real SSE socket
disconnect — POST /api/chat-runs not wired or Hono server down
mock — EventSource mocked to emit a canned string with no durable row

steps: type 'What is two plus two?' in the chat composer

must_observe: >=1 SSE `token` events received (each a `data:` line with a `{token}` payload)
each token appends to a single in-progress assistant bubble (assistant bubble count `1`)
the bubble text grows character-by-character until the `terminal` event
must_not_observe: multiple assistant bubbles for one reply (count `>1`)
the full reply appearing instantly with `0` token-by-token buildup

would_fail_if: disconnect — reconnect replays ALL events from seq=0, duplicating tokens
stub — reconnect resumes from a cached array, no real Last-Event-ID header
mock — EventSource mocked to replay all events on reconnect
empty — Last-Event-ID header not sent on reconnect

steps: send a message that triggers a streaming reply (>=5 tokens)
toggle airplane mode ON for 3 seconds
wait for the stream to resume and complete

must_observe: the stream resumes after reconnect (new tokens arrive, count `>0`)
`0` duplicate tokens in the final assistant message (token count `==` unique token count)
the final message text matches the durable Zero-synced `chat_messages.content` row
must_not_observe: duplicate token strings appearing (e.g. `FourFour` instead of `Four`)
multiple assistant bubbles for one reply (count `>1`)
a spinner with no message after completion (count `0` messages)
the stream not resuming (stalled at `3` tokens, `0` new tokens)

would_fail_if: disconnect — durable row not written to Postgres
empty — Zero query returns no row for the message
stub — thread shows a hardcoded string with no durable row
mock — terminal event faked, no real chat_messages row written

steps: send a message from the chat composer
wait for the streaming reply to complete (terminal event received)

must_observe: `1` final assistant message bubble rendered (count exactly `1`)
the bubble text equals the Zero `chat_messages.content` value (diff `== 0`)
the Zero query returns `1` row with `role='agent'`
the bubble count stays `1` after the state transitions to `complete`
must_not_observe: more than `1` final assistant bubble for the reply
a spinner with no message (count `0` messages)
the bubble text differing from the Zero row (diff `>0`)

would_fail_if: disconnect — Last-Event-ID header not sent on reconnect
stub — gap-fill is a no-op, missing tokens never arrive
mock — server mocked to replay all events from seq=0
empty — reconnect starts a new stream without gap-fill

steps: send a message that triggers a streaming reply (>=8 tokens)
wait for 3 tokens to arrive (note the seq id, e.g. id:3)
toggle airplane mode ON for 3 seconds
toggle airplane mode OFF (trigger reconnect with Last-Event-ID=3)
wait for the stream to complete

must_observe: the final message token count `==` the server total token event count
the Zero `chat_messages.content` equals the assembled streamed text (diff `== 0`)
must_not_observe: the final message has fewer tokens than expected (gap-fill failed, count `<` total)
`0` unique tokens in the final message (empty)

would_fail_if: stub — cancel is a no-op, streaming continues
empty — cancel button does not trigger state transition
mock — cancel mocked to succeed without calling the server

steps: send a message that triggers a streaming reply (>=8 tokens)

must_observe: `0` further SSE token events after cancel (stream stops)
the state machine transitions to the `cancelled` state
must_not_observe: streaming continues after cancel (`>0` further tokens)
the partial message disappears (count `0` tokens shown)
the state remains in the `streaming` state (not `cancelled`)
